Update with SLOOS overlay:
- Credit supply and demand: SLOOS shows broad easing of standards and stronger demand for C&I across large, middle‑market, and small firms, with more credit line inquiries and demand tied to customer investment. Standards also eased for CRE (construction, land development, nonfarm nonresidential, multifamily). These are supportive for near‑term business activity and investment.
- Household credit: Despite some easing in consumer standards (credit card, auto, HELOCs, jumbo), banks reported weaker demand for residential real estate loans (including GSE and subprime) and expect deterioration in household credit performance (credit card, auto, nonconforming jumbo) as rates rise—tempering the outlook.
- Rates and policy: Banks expect higher interest rates, aligning with the FOMC’s imminent liftoff and end of net purchases. Tightening policy will gradually offset currently accommodative financial conditions.
- Risk backdrop and resilience: The Financial Stability Report flags elevated vulnerabilities (rich valuations, duration risk, liquidity mismatches, nonbank leverage, Treasury market fragilities), while bank capital/liquidity and household balance sheets remain solid buffers.

Net tone: SLOOS tilts the assessment modestly more positive for growth via business credit and CRE, but softer RRE/consumer dynamics and the policy‑normalization path keep the balance only slightly positive.
